subject: Proposed SLA attribution for customer-managed peering — Havenbrook
messages:
From: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@havenbrook.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Aug 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA carveout request: customer-managed peering and edge routers

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week — we appreciated the walkthrough. As we move to finalize the Dedicated/Private deployment terms, our legal and network teams have asked for a narrowly scoped exception to Redwood's uptime SLA for traffic that transits our customer-managed peering and edge routing equipment.

Specifically, we propose the following:
1) Exclude loss of availability/latency attributable to customer-owned peering (BGP sessions at our edge) and on-prem edge routers from Redwood's 99.9% per-month availability calculation.
2) Redwood will provide an attribution protocol that includes incident timelines, redacted server-level logs, and path-level traceroutes within 48 hours of request.
3) Both parties will adopt an operational fallback policy: when Redwood detects an upstream customer-side outage, Redwood will attempt routing fallback to a secondary peering path where available. Responsibility for customer-side cost and time to provision alternate paths remains with Havenbrook.

Action items we need from Redwood: suggested contract wording for the carveout, a short list of monitoring evidence you can provide during root cause analysis (RCA), and a proposed attribution matrix (example: percent responsibility by problem class).

I can share a template redline from our counsel if helpful. We'd like to get a first-pass answer this week so procurement can move the contract to signature.

Thanks,
Jorge Alvarez
Director, Cloud Operations
Havenbrook Systems
Attachment: (none)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Hi Jorge — thanks for laying this out clearly. I appreciate the narrow scope you described; makes the negotiation straightforward.

Looping in Logan (CS) and Marcus (SE) to validate the operational suggestions, and Soojin from Legal to draft an initial contract amendment.

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus: sketch an attribution matrix and list the monitoring artifacts we can reliably provide.
- Soojin: produce a 1-2 paragraph contract carveout draft for review (we'll attach to the managed services appendix).
- Logan: propose how this affects our runbook and on-call escalation for private deployments.

Can you do a short sync tomorrow at 11am PT? If not, propose two alternatives. If you send your counsel's template redline, we'll ingest it and send a counter-redline within 48 hours.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

On Thu, Aug 2, 2028 at 9:15 AM Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@havenbrook.com> wrote:
> Specifically, we propose the following:
> 1) Exclude loss of availability/latency attributable to customer-owned peering (BGP sessions at our edge) and on-prem edge routers from Redwood's 99.9% per-month availability calculation.

Hi Jorge / Grace — quick technical note from the SE side. We're aligned with keeping the carveout tight; a couple of practical suggestions to make attribution deterministic so both sides can sign off quickly:

1) Define clear detection signals:
   - Customer-side BGP flap with origin AS path change + simultaneous traceroute divergence to >= 50% of our egress POPs.
   - Customer edge counter increments (interface down/up) corroborated by our Active Healthcheck failures to the customer demarc during the same window.
2) Evidence package we can reliably produce:
   - Redwood ingress POP metrics (per-POP latency and packet loss) for impacted prefixes (7-day retention by default, 30-day on request).
   - Aggregated traceroutes and BGP table snapshots at time of incident.
   - Correlated request traces showing increased tail latency where applicable.
3) Attribution matrix (attached as SLA-ATtribution-Matrix.csv) — sample rows map: \"BGP flap at customer edge\" => \"customer responsibility 100%\"; \"Redwood mis-announcement\" => \"redwood responsibility 100%\"; \"intermediate transit provider\" => \"shared (investigation)\".
4) Fallback behavior: we can implement an automatic fallback attempt where a secondary peering path exists, but only if the customer authorizes automatic announcements to the secondary AS and accepts potential transient route churn as a trade-off. We should add an opt-in field in the onboarding checklist.

I'll attach the attribution matrix (CSV) for legal/ops to review. Happy to jump on the 11am PT slot.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla-attribution-matrix.csv
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@havenbrook.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 04 Aug 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA carveout request: customer-managed peering and edge routers

Hi Jorge / team — thanks for the patience while Legal reviewed Marcus's notes and the sample matrix. Attached is a draft amendment (havenbrook-sla-amendment-draft.pdf) with the following highlights:

- Narrow carveout language limited to on-prem peerings and customer-owned edge routing devices (defined in Appendix A).
- Evidence requirements: Redwood will deliver the evidence package described by Marcus within 48 hours of formal request; exceptions only for redacted customer data.
- Fallback/opt-in: language requires customer opt-in for automatic fallback routing; opt-in must be documented in the onboarding checklist and can be toggled by the customer.
- Retention & audit: evidence retained for 90 days by default; longer retention requires purchasing extended observability add-on.
- Dispute resolution: an expedited review window (5 business days) with a joint postmortem and binding attribution determination based on the agreed matrix.

Two legal caveats for your consideration:
1) We cannot accept open-ended indemnification arising from customer-side misconfiguration; recommend a mutual limitation clause.
2) If the customer requires extended retention or decrypted packet captures as evidence, that will require a separate data processing addendum and potentially additional fees.

If you confirm you want these terms, I'll prepare a DocuSign package. DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/mock/preview/DRFT-4592.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: havenbrook-sla-amendment-draft.pdf
